Ace: Out of aces?

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Could the State Capture saga finally be nearing a tipping point as Ace Magashule, one of the most influential players in South Africa's worst political scandal to date faces his accusers in court?

Unique Selling Point:
Former Free State Premier and current ANC Secretary General Ace Magashule will reportedly appear in the Bloemfontein Magistrates Court on friday 13 November to face charges of corruption brought under the Prevention and Combatting of Corrupt Activities Act. He is also expected to be arrested at the same time. This comes after years of allegations against Magashule, implicating him in a variety of questionable deals and accusing him of using his political influence to allow corruption and state capture.

Summary:
Over the years we have done many stories where allegations of corruption have surfaced against Magashule, from the notorious Estina Dairy Farm to touching on the Asbestos Audit scam he is currently accused of. We even had allegations against him as far back as 2013, in my story Brother Zuma's Billions, where Jacob Zuma's brother, Michael Zuma, admitted he had received money from a company called Khumbula to get tenders awarded from the Free State Government and then Premier Ace Magashule. Script Extract:

Devi Sankaree Govender (Carte Blanche presenter): “Did you go to Bloemfontein to get the tender for Khumbula?”
Voice of Michael Zuma: “I did go, yes.”
Devi: “And who did you see in Bloemfontein?”
Voice of Michael Zuma: “No, I’ve seen the big boss for there, ‘Ace’ Magashule.”
Devi: “The Premier of the province?”
Voice of Michael Zuma: “I spoke to them. Ja, I spoke to him. He’s a comrade.”
Devi: “And then Michael, what did you say to ‘Ace’? Did you say ‘I need to get a tender for housing’ or how do you approach it, what do you say?”
Voice of Michael Zuma: “I said I need a job... I said I need a job. For housing. I want to do housing.”
Devi: “Did you tell ‘Ace’ that you were phoning on behalf of Khumbula?”
Voice of Michael Zuma: “Yes, yes.”

The question now is what does his imminent arrest and subsequent trial mean for the political future of the ANC, Magashule's own political career, and despite the many allegations over the years, will the NPA's case be strong enough to prove his guilt? In a country desperate for the people behind state capture to finally be held accountable, could the arrest of one of the ANC's top six be the tipping point to some long awaited justice?

Further information:
- We will have to have a camera man in Bloemfontein tomorrow. Evert Kleinhans is available. Tony Beamish has requested permission to film from the Magistrate - the magistrate has answered and advised all media houses that the court cannot accommodate the amount of journalists requesting permission, and that media houses should arrange a pool feed amongst themselves. SANEF is coordinating this.

- We have many of our past inserts to use for background

- Except for the usual analysts, we could ask Magashule's former ally and former Free State Economic Development MEC Mxolisi Dukwana, who has testified at the Zondo commission and spoken out against Magashule in public recently, for an interview

SUGGESTED TREATMENT
A news piece providing an in depth look at why the case is such a big story, and the events leading up to it. The angle is two fold: Political analysis of what this means for the ANC and the ongoing factional wars inside the party, as well as posing the question of whether we are finally starting to see the long awaited cleaning up of the State Capture saga.

Script:


Ace out of Aces
First Draft Script
19 November 2020

Voice
On friday last week, former Free State Premier and current ANC Secretary General Ace Magashule appeared in the Bloemfontein Magistrates Court on 21 charges of corruption and fraud, alternatively theft and money laundering. He was charged for his alleged involvement in what the state claims is a fraudulent R255 million contract for the assessment and removal of asbestos roofs on houses in the Free State Province.
According to an NPA statement, some of the charges against Magashule relating to the asbestos deal include:
that he corruptly accepted gratification of R 53 550-00, paid on his request towards the tuition fees of the daughter of a then acting judge,
that a payment of R 250 000-00, on his request, was made to a travel agency towards the travel expenses of a delegation to Cuba.
and that he failed to report corrupt transactions in contravention of the Prevention and Combating of Corrupt Activities Act.
He was released on R200 000 bail and ordered to surrender his passport to the authorities.

Link Masa
He’s only expected back in court in February next year, and the trial is one of the first high profile cases linked to state capture the country has seen. Will this be a watershed moment in ANC politics?

Voice
The National Prosecuting Authority acts independently of other organs of state - they don’t do the president’s bidding. Political analyst Professor Mcebisi Ndletyana says this development nevertheless shows that President Cyril Ramaphosa was being serious when he penned an extraordinary letter to ANC branches in August this year, condemning corruption and saying the party was accused nr 1 when it came to questions of graft.

Sound Up Prof Ndletyana
Masa: Is this an all out fight between President Cyril Ramaphosa and Ace Magashule as has been speculated?

Prof: It is.

Masa: It’s a showdown?

Prof: It’s a showdown. It’s the ultimate showdown. If he knocks this hurdle down, it will have a domino effect. Everyone like him will follow. Because you have killed the king. So all the acolytes of the king, will follow.

Voice
Despite the serious charges levelled against him, a number of prominent ANC members, including Malusi Gigaba, Supra Mahumapelo, Carl Neihaus, and Tony Yengeni arrived at court on friday, together with a large crowd of party supporters.
Magashule’s real support started in 2009, when newly elected president Jacob Zuma gave him the premiership of the Free State.

Sound Up Prof Ndletyana
Ace and JZ are part of the same whatsapp group. It goes back to 2005 / 2006, because Ace was one of the first provincial leaders to support JZ when he was fired by Thabo Mbeki.




Voice
During his 9 years as premier of the Free State, there were many allegations that Magashule used his position of power to turn the province into a patronage network, built on a culture of fear. Mxolisi Dukwana is a former Free State MEC and comrade of Magashule’s. Last year he testified under oath at the Zondo Commision of inquiry, detailing how the Gupta’s allegedly bribed the former Premier.

Sound Up Mxolisi Dukwana
I drive there to Mr Ace Magashule’s place, and I give him his million.

Voice
The Gupta’s have been linked to Magashule through the failed Vrede Dairy Farm project in the Free State, which allegedly saw R340 million rand end up in the hands of the Gupta’s and their associates. Magashule protested his innocence, and welcomed the Hawks investigation into the matter.

Sound Up Ace Magashule
Wherever there is corruption, the law must take it’s place. Whether it’s with Vrede dairy or any other thing.

Sound Up Mxolisi Dukwana
We have had toxic leadership for quite a long time in the Free State, at the helm of that toxic leadership has been Ace Magashule.

Voice
Allegations of the corrupt Asbestos Housing deal, which Magashule has now been charged for, first came to light in journalist and author Pieter-Louis Myburgh’s book, Gangster State.

Sound Up Pieter-Louis Myburgh
he undeniably acted like a fully fledged gangster, in a position of power.

Voice
The allegedly corrupt tender, valued at R255 million rand, drained the coffers of the Free State’s Human Settlements Department. It was an audit, to determine which Free State Houses had asbestos roofs. Tenderpreneur Igo Mpanbani was one of the people appointed to do the job in 2014. Myburgh said he had evidence to show that Mpanbani was Magashule’s bagman.

Sound Up Myburgh
R10 million, R15 million, R20 million. The money keeps on flushing into Igo Mpanbani’s pockets. At key moments, Ace Magashule’s PA’s then contact Mpanbani, via email, and tell him how to spend the money in certain ways, on the instruction of Ace Magashule.

Voice
Last year we met Rathipe Molupi from Kutlenong - he was one of the ward councillors asked to count the houses with asbestos roofs.

Sound Up Molupi
Molupi: We did the count, I mean it’s easy, you just walk past the house, you don’t have to go inside the house.

Devi: You can see it?

Molupi: you can see it, just walking or driving past.

Devi: Do you think that project was worth R255 million?

Molupi: No I think the project is worth zero rands, or zero million rands. So it just went down the drain.

Voice
Mpanbani won’t be one of the 12 accused to stand trial with Magashule when the case resumes next year. In 2017 he was assassinated, his body found next to his Bentley which reportedly contained a million rand in cash.

Magashule did not respond to our request for an interview for this story, and his attorney told us he had advised his client not to speak to the media as the matter is sub judice.

Sound Up Peter Louis Myburgh.
This is a previously untold scandal on the scale of the Vrede dairy scandal.

Voice
Adressing his supporters outside of court after his bail hearing, Magashule blamed it all on a political conspiracy against him.

Constitutional law expert Professor Pierre de Vos says those claims would have to be backed up by solid evidence.

Sound Up Prof Pierre de Vos
But unlike in the court of public opinion, in the court of law you have to being evidence. The problem with all these claims of conspiracy is that they are made without any substantiating evidence. And so this might be convincing in the political sphere, but in the actual court room it is going to have no impact on the outcome of the case.

Voice
Professor de Vos says of the 21 charges Magashule will face in court, the most serious is corruption.

Sound Up Prof Pierre de Vos
Because there’s a minimum sentence of 15 years if you are found guilty, unless there are exceptional circumstances to make that less. So the charges are actually rather serious.

Link Masa
Commentators have for many years now called the ANC a deeply divided party, and critics have blamed the political in-fighting for many of the organisations failures in the past. How the African National Congress handles the corruption trial of one of their Top 6, will have a lasting impact on the country’s future.

Voice
At their previous National Conference, the ANC adopted a resolution that members accused of corruption should step down. But Magashule has so far refused to do so.
requests for comment from the party’s national spokesperson Pule Mabe went unanswered, but Professor Ndletyana believes the party’s National Executive Committee will ultimately make the call.

Sound Up Prof Ndletyana
the logical consequence of that therefore should be Ace must step down.

Voice
The rule of law is key to a healthy democracy, and Ndletyana says every South African should be supporting the current court process, irrespective of the outcome.

Sound Up Prof Ndletyana
So this is a test, about how much we detest this immorality that has contaminated our society.



Ace out of aces Promos

Promo 1
It’s been years in the making, ANC Secretary General Ace Magashule will finally face allegations of fraud and corruption in a court of law, but how will this effect an already divided ruling party?

Promo 2
We revisit ANC Secretary General Ace Magashule’s journey in the Free State, and what the case that’s landed him in court on charges of corruption means for the ruling party and the country as a whole.

Promo 3
ANC Secretary General Ace Magashule under fire as he fights for both his personal and political future after being charged with fraud, corruption and money laundering - we take a closer look at the case.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Former Free State Premier and current ANC Secretary General Ace Magashule will reportedly appear in the Bloemfontein Magistrates Court on friday 13 November to face charges of corruption brought under the Prevention and Combatting of Corrupt Activities Act. He is also expected to be arrested at the same time. This comes after years of allegations against Magashule, implicating him in a variety of questionable deals and accusing him of using his political influence to allow corruption and state capture.
metadata.Summary: Over the years we have done many stories where allegations of corruption have surfaced against Magashule, from the notorious Estina Dairy Farm to touching on the Asbestos Audit scam he is currently accused of. We even had allegations against him as far back as 2013, in my story Brother Zuma's Billions, where Jacob Zuma's brother, Michael Zuma, admitted he had received money from a company called Khumbula to get tenders awarded from the Free State Government and then Premier Ace Magashule. Script Extract: Devi Sankaree Govender (Carte Blanche presenter): “Did you go to Bloemfontein to get the tender for Khumbula?” Voice of Michael Zuma: “I did go, yes.” Devi: “And who did you see in Bloemfontein?” Voice of Michael Zuma: “No, I’ve seen the big boss for there, ‘Ace’ Magashule.” Devi: “The Premier of the province?” Voice of Michael Zuma: “I spoke to them. Ja, I spoke to him. He’s a comrade.” Devi: “And then Michael, what did you say to ‘Ace’? Did you say ‘I need to get a tender for housing’ or how do you approach it, what do you say?” Voice of Michael Zuma: “I said I need a job... I said I need a job. For housing. I want to do housing.” Devi: “Did you tell ‘Ace’ that you were phoning on behalf of Khumbula?” Voice of Michael Zuma: “Yes, yes.” The question now is what does his imminent arrest and subsequent trial mean for the political future of the ANC, Magashule's own political career, and despite the many allegations over the years, will the NPA's case be strong enough to prove his guilt? In a country desperate for the people behind state capture to finally be held accountable, could the arrest of one of the ANC's top six be the tipping point to some long awaited justice?
metadata.Further information: - We will have to have a camera man in Bloemfontein tomorrow. Evert Kleinhans is available. Tony Beamish has requested permission to film from the Magistrate - the magistrate has answered and advised all media houses that the court cannot accommodate the amount of journalists requesting permission, and that media houses should arrange a pool feed amongst themselves. SANEF is coordinating this. - We have many of our past inserts to use for background - Except for the usual analysts, we could ask Magashule's former ally and former Free State Economic Development MEC Mxolisi Dukwana, who has testified at the Zondo commission and spoken out against Magashule in public recently, for an interview SUGGESTED TREATMENT A news piece providing an in depth look at why the case is such a big story, and the events leading up to it. The angle is two fold: Political analysis of what this means for the ANC and the ongoing factional wars inside the party, as well as posing the question of whether we are finally starting to see the long awaited cleaning up of the State Capture saga.
